thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — int8 bringup for newmodel-x produced a spike in low-quality replies across the promptbank. Posting a couple noisy examples and a short triage plan.

sam: Ugh, saw similar on the qbench dashboard. Do you have a minimal repro prompt?

maya: Yep — two small repros below. baseline is newmodel-x fp16, suspect is int8 distillation.

maya: ```
prompt: 'Summarize the policy in plain language.'
fp16: 'The policy requires users to verify identity and may restrict access under section 3.2.'
int8: 'You must do some stuff with identity, sometimes banned, see section.'

prompt: 'How to reset password for a corporate account?'
fp16: 'Use the SSO portal, follow steps 1-3, contact IT if MFA fails.'
int8: 'Go to settings, click reset, if broken call support maybe.'
```

jordan: Those are lower fidelity and more terse, not just length. Could be tokenization change + reorder from quant kernels. Any tokenization diffs between builds?

lee: I ran embed-recall for the same prompts and saw a 12% drop in paraphrase recall for the int8 run (micro-bucket: paraphrase-heavy). Path: s3://redwood/qbench/newmodel-x/int8/recall-vs-fp16.json

sam: Tokenizer version is the same AFAICT, but the kernel patch swapped softmax implementation earlier this week. cc @ops-bot for the rollout provenance.

ops-bot: Deploy log: newmodel-x-int8 rolled to staging at 2025-11-09T14:03Z (build 20251109.3). Kernel patch id: k-77b2.

maya: OK — working hypothesis: quant kernel change + int8 calibration produced subtle distributional shifts that affect paraphrase/conciseness. Plan: 1) build prompt subset (1k) of paraphrase-heavy examples, 2) dedupe + deid check, 3) relabel golden for 200 examples, 4) run targeted qbench metrics and high-sensitivity eval.

jordan: For step 1, suggest stratified sampling across these buckets: paraphrase-heavy, instruction-rewrite, and safety-edge. I can wire up the sampler if you give the sample sizes.

maya: Target sizes: paraphrase-heavy 1k, instruction-rewrite 400, safety-edge 200. Use seed 20251109 and include metadata fields: prompt_id, tokenizer_hash, orig_model_score.

sam: Dedupe note — we should run the new fuzzyhash v2 (handles punctuation variants). Command I used locally: 
``` 
python tools/sample.py --promptset s3://redwood/promptbank/v3 --buckets paraphrase,instruction,safety --out ./tmp/sample.json --seed 20251109 --fuzzy v2
```

labelbot: Creating label tasks for 200 golden relabels (priority: high). Assigning to pool: curation-1. Expected ETA: 48h. Link: https://labelflow/internal/tasks/label/NT-8923

lee: Also recommend short manual pass for the paraphrase cohort to verify token splits. I've seen int8 merge word pieces oddly when punctuation is dense.

maya: Good call. Jordan — can you surface the tokenizer diffs and produce a small tokenization comparison artifact for a 500-sample holdout? That will help us rule tokenization vs kernel.

jordan: On it. I'll push a small report to the qbench artifact bucket by EOD.

sam: Once the golden relabels are in, we should run two evals: high-sensitivity scoring (A/B with MRR+BLEU-ish heuristics) and a human-blind comparison to catch brevity regressions. I can script the A/B today.

maya: Timeline: today — generate sample and dedupe, ops confirm kernel provenance (done), label tasks created (done), tomorrow — relabels + tokenization diff report, then targeted qbench run and triage call after results.

ops-bot: Note: fallback image — we can roll back int8 to previous kernel (k-75a1) within 30 mins if regression persists. Use rollback-tag: newmodel-x-int8-k75a1

labelbot: Relabel batch created: NT-8923. 200 tasks assigned, expectation 48h. Ping @maya when complete.

maya: Thanks all. Final ask: keep examples of systematic brevity or safety word-drop in a shared doc (I'll create one). Anyone seeing patterns, paste example lines and label severity low/med/high.

sam: I'll monitor qbench graphs and post any other spikes to this thread. :eyes:

jordan: Tokenizer diff report uploaded: s3://redwood/qbench/newmodel-x/int8/token-diff-report-1719012345.json

lee: Quick note — I flagged 12 items that look like punctuation collapse; adding them to the relabeler attachments.

maya: Awesome. We'll reconvene after relabels + qbench run. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
